summary: On one MI350X/gfx950, three representative BF16 convolutions were 1.37x to 1.71x slower than preallocated Torch BF16 GEMMs with the same implicit-GEMM dimensions. The current 32x32 heuristic tile was fastest across the complete shipped 32/64/128 ladder for all three shapes, so no unjustified production tuning change was made.

tests.what_was_measured: GPU-event timings for three current FlyDSL public convolution calls, all three shipped tile-ladder choices, equivalent preallocated Torch BF16 GEMMs, and independent Torch convolution accuracy. Raw 100-sample distributions are retained.
Focused GPU correctness coverage for all eight explicit tile configurations (8 passed).

gpu_execution_evidence: raw_measurements.json records AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950, GPU index 0, unique ID 0x6e4208b780600d88, GPU-event samples, and successful independent numerical comparisons.
remaining_limitations: Only three small repository-test-derived shapes were measured, not a full model trace.
Torch GEMM is a compute-density reference and has a different memory-access pattern from implicit convolution.
Public-call timing includes allocation and dispatch, so the observed gap is not attributed solely to MFMA execution.
No compiler defect or justified improvement within the current tile ladder was demonstrated; broader kernel design work remains unverified.
